content.comment_body: Hello, I need assistance because I can't save my project in [product_name] after making any modifications. I've included the [document] for review, hoping someone can identify the issue in one of the LSC files. After testing on different computers, the result is always the same: I can't save after a small change (for example, moving a text object slightly). I'm uncertain how to solve this. If there is a [product_name] expert here, I'd appreciate help.
Have you tried running your [product_name] program with administrator privileges on your laptop?

Your project file is corrupted. The Ethernet connection between your PLC device and the panel cannot be opened or deleted, and there may be other errors present. I recommend submitting a support request and providing your project file to [company_name] for investigation.
Yes, I tried running it as an administrator, but I still cannot save.

Here is the response from [company_name] Support. Does anyone know how to copy PLC connections from one project to another? Dear Mr [user_name], I was able to replicate the issue: using “save as…” does not save the project file. All diagrams can still be read, so I tried to pinpoint the defect. Since many Ethernet connections cannot be deleted, it's likely they're damaged. This project file cannot be repaired. A possible solution is to create a new project and copy the diagrams and connections into it. Best regards, Your Technical Support for Industry Automation and Drive Technologies [snip]

Hello, I've rebuilt the project. I exported the relevant diagrams as individual files and then imported them into a new project. The inter-device connections were retained, but I had to delete and recreate the panel connections. Please check these connections, particularly regarding TSAPs. In my view, there might be one connection too many, since a base panel can only manage four connections.
Thank you. As mentioned in my initial message, I needed an expert to help. [user_name], you truly are that expert. I tested the rebuilt project last night and it now saves and works correctly.
In my experience, corrupted network projects are often caused by faulty connections between devices.

analysis.insight_summary: The main concern is that corrupted files in [product_name] can prevent users from saving changes, even minor ones, disrupting workflows. This issue occurs on multiple computers, suggesting file integrity problems likely related to defective Ethernet connections. Users were frustrated by the absence of direct troubleshooting or automated recovery options, and had to manually rebuild projects as a workaround.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to reliably save changes to their projects, even after minor edits, and would like robust recovery options or troubleshooting assistance when files are corrupted.
